items.claim: A transition never ends when its tween is canceled from outside (`cancelKey`, `cancelAll`) or a tick throws
items.note: It needed a new public tween option in the animator package, outside the d3 area: `onCancel`, added in 90aa1cae79 with a `minor` changeset.

items.claim: Two scenes on one animator interrupt each other's nodes that share an id
items.note: `transitionCancelKey` now takes the scene as its first argument. That function is unreleased, so I edited its existing changeset instead of adding a breaking one.

items.claim: A second transition on a selection snaps nodes back to their pose before the join, and a second one under another name with no `.pose()` pins the pose
items.note: Only the first transition to start on a node after its join tweens it from the prior pose.

items.claim: An interrupted item counts as done, so a later `.remove()` deletes the node and a later chained transition restarts it
A chain item queued on a microtask still runs after it is interrupted and kills the newer transition
A `join()` that throws has already canceled the pending exit removals
items.note: All mappers now run before anything changes, so a mapper that throws changes nothing either.

items.claim: `start` fires, and starting values are read, before the delay ends
Two `.tween()` calls with the same name hang the transition
items.note: The later one replaces the earlier, as d3 does. This is a behavior call nobody had made, so it is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: A missing `lerp` throws only after the transition is marked scheduled, so a second `end()` never settles; it also throws for transitions that tween no pose
`delay(NaN)` silently starts at once while `duration(NaN)` throws
items.note: A constant `NaN` now throws a `RangeError` where it is set. A delay function that returns `NaN` warns and starts the item at once. This call is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: An entering datum's `.pose()` is called twice, so a random pose tweens instead of snapping in
An item with nothing to tween ended at once, where d3 lasts its duration
items.note: My dc26fd25cc fix had exposed this.

items.claim: My new edge tests' clock had no `now`, so the animator read wall time and the tests were flaky
Two `.tween()` calls with one name on a transition hang it: the second cancels the first without its `onDone`
A dropped item counts as "done" for anything added after the drop: a later child runs it, and a later `.remove()` deletes an interrupted node
Sibling chained transitions (`t.transition()` called twice) cancel each other's pose tween silently, so the first never ends
`'start'` fires when the first item is scheduled, before its delay has passed, and even when that item is canceled during the delay
`schedule` marks the stage scheduled and arms `.remove()` before refusing a descriptor without `lerp`, which leaves stale state after the throw
A root transition with only custom tweens still tweens the pose, and a concurrent named one can leave nodes at their pre-join pose
A deferred item of a chained transition runs after it was interrupted
Canceling a transition's tween through the exported cancel key, or `animator.cancelAll()`, strands the transition
A transition that starts late interrupts a newer transition of the same name that is still waiting out its delay
